options: A single order line picked in complete isolation
A batch of released lines grouped together for efficient warehouse picking, often by ship date or carrier
questions.explain: A pick wave groups released lines together, letting the warehouse plan an efficient picking run rather than handling one line at a time.

questions.q: What does confirming a pick task do in the system?
options: Decrements the available quantity at that storage location and marks the task complete
questions.explain: Confirming a pick task reduces the available inventory at that location and marks the pick as done.

options: An order with only one line
A situation where fewer units are actually available to pick than the order requires
questions.explain: A short pick occurs when the quantity actually available to pull from inventory is less than what was ordered.

questions.q: What does the packing step record?
options: Which picked items were grouped into which shippable containers, including counts, weights, and dimensions
The General Ledger account for revenue
questions.explain: Packing records how picked items are grouped into containers, which feeds shipping documentation and freight calculation.

questions.q: What is the final step after an order is picked, packed, and staged?
options: Immediate posting to the General Ledger
Ship confirmation, the step that tells the system the goods actually left
questions.explain: After staging, ship confirmation records that the shipment actually left, covered in the next lesson.
